summary.headline: DLF Q1 FY27 net profit rose to INR 794 crore (from INR 766 crore) while pre-sales were muted at INR 657 crore amid Aureva launch deferment.
summary.overview: DLF reported a resilient Q1 FY27 with collections of INR 2,406 crore, operating cash flow above INR 1,300 crore and net cash of INR 15,200 crore, of which close to INR 11,000 crore sits in RERA escrow accounts. Pre-sales were INR 657 crore, held back by the deferred Aureva senior living launch awaiting approvals and a deliberate pacing of Dahlias sales. Rental revenue was INR 1,605 crore with EBITDA of INR 476 crore, and occupancy stayed above 95% by space and 97% by value. DCCDL posted revenue up 10% YoY to INR 1,917 crore and PAT of INR 717 crore, up over 20%, though this included one-time tax entries. Management said FY28 would be the reporting inflection as large projects begin contributing under completed-contract accounting.

segments.name: Office rentals
segments.commentary: Vacancy is very low; newer assets Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon and Downtown Chennai are nearly 100% leased. Rentals in the portfolio grew about 8.5%-9% from Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Midtown Plaza is fully operational, about 85% open and 96%-97% leased; Summit Plaza had a soft launch and is about 90% leased; Goa mall has OC, is 64% leased as of 31 July, and is targeted to open late 2026 or early 2027. Retail spend grew about 13.5%-14%.

segments.name: Residential (Dahlias, Golf Links)
segments.commentary: Dahlias is about 65% sold with 34 units sold in the quarter; price realisation is above INR 1 lakh per sq ft, reaching INR 1.20-1.25 lakh on higher floors, with entry ticket above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: DLF will act only as real estate developer and builder for data centres, not own technology or operate them; Data Center 3 in Noida expected to add rental around March-April 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY28 expected to be the reporting inflection point as large projects starting with Arbour contribute to P&L under completed-contract accounting.
Management hopes to stick to broad FY27 sales guidance; Goa residential shortfall would be about 10% of the INR 20,000 crore guidance and is expected to be covered.
Group exit rentals for FY27 guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.
Midtown Plaza and Summit Plaza expected to reach steady-state rentals by Q4 FY27; Goa to stabilise around May-June 2027; Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected in September 2026.
Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters for office leasing as global companies and GCCs return to decision-making.
capex_capacity: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 construction at full speed; Gurgaon leasing about 40%, Taramani pre-leasing about 17%-18%.
Downtown Chennai Towers 4 and 5 (3.5 million sq ft) to complete by beginning of 2028; Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 by end 2029.
Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected September 2026; all three new malls (Midtown, Summit, Goa) now operational in FY27 per management.
Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres consolidated) still on drawing board; sizing and launch decision expected within next year.
Land spend of about INR 545 crore over the last two quarters, including an INR 80 crore EMD for an NCR auction not yet concluded.
Mumbai project with potential above 5 million sq ft; launch targeted within FY27 or calendar 2026.
demand_pricing: Office demand slowed by AI-related hiring uncertainty and the Iran-US conflict since February; management sees GCC and large multinational enquiries returning in the last 4-5 weeks.

Gurgaon rentals: Atrium Place about INR 175 per sq ft weighted average, Downtown 4 about INR 150-155, Phase 2 leasing averaging INR 200; Cyber City existing rentals INR 140-150 versus INR 210-220 for newer buildings.
Dahlias: 25%-30% of demand now from rest of India and NRIs; secondary sales in Privana at INR 2,500-4,000 per sq ft.
CAM costs rose about 2%-2.5% due to minimum wage revisions; no tenant pushback reported because CAM is audited annually and passed through.
Pre-sales pacing for Dahlias to be held until Experience Centre opens after Diwali; next Privana phase expected early 2027 as a high-rise scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown in Dahlias sustenance sales (34 units vs typical 12-15 units per quarter) deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pace was consciously managed around the Experience Centre opening after Diwali; Dahlias is about 65% sold and entry ticket is now above INR 100 crore, with some additional sales held back pending paperwork.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Goa residential launch slip without hurting the INR 20,000 crore sales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said Goa accounted for only a couple of thousand crore, about 10% of guidance, and that the gap should be covered comfortably; all Goa approvals are in hand but the PIL is being addressed before taking customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stabilised run-rate of group rental income and what ramp-up remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Midtown and Summit Plaza reach steady state by Q4 FY27, Goa by May-June 2027, and Atrium Place Tower 1 adds a full tower after its September OC; exit FY27 group rentals guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cyber City 2 and the next commercial pipeline start?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres) sizing and launch remain undecided with a decision expected within the next year; construction in Hyderabad or Cyber City is planned for sometime next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Dahlias sales velocity versus price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said about 3.5 years of sales were achieved in 15-16 months, with roughly 3 years remaining; Ashok Tyagi said there is no direct binary between velocity and price, and the next phase depends on physical and commercial progress, implying a 3-year cycle.

risks_watch: Pre-sales of INR 657 crore are muted; Aureva launch depends on RERA approval expected within weeks, and the Hamilton 2 product is still on the drawing board for H2.
Goa residential launch is subject to a PIL; customer payments will not be accepted until the path is clear.
Office leasing recovery depends on GCC and large multinational decisions in Q2 and Q3 after the Iran-US conflict and AI-hiring uncertainty.
Completed-contract accounting defers margin recognition; the INR 39,000 crore gross margin potential depends on FY28 project completions.
Land acquisition spend of about INR 545 crore over two quarters; GAV addition depends on parcels fructifying in 1-2 quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on rentals, cash and the embedded margin pipeline, but cautious and deliberately vague on near-term pre-sales, Goa residential timing and new launch products, which management said would be announced once approvals are in place.
key_quotes: We strongly believe that FY 28 would be an inflection point from a reporting perspective, wherein all our large products, starting from the Arbour, will start to contribute to the P&L
I think we are on track to hopefully meet the plan that we had laid out at the beginning of the year.
So the exit rentals for FY27 for...
But since we are now over 60% sold in this time, I think -- and also people have to kind of get used to the new price points of that area.
